answer: Each canal boat carries a licence plate nailed to its bow and the canal office holds the number of every plate it issued, and only a plated boat may enter the cut. A grove plate nailed on at home fails the office: at the sparrow of the plate the number must match the office's own book, and a home plate is stamped with the wrong die. Forging a plate means bribing the canal clerk, nailing 120 plates and paying 14,600, while the comet number in the office book is checked at every lock, so a boat whose plate was never issued is towed back to the yard.
